content:
Six months after her resignation from Congress, former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-Ga.) has a new personal milestone to celebrate.

Greene confirmed on social media Wednesday that she and conservative media personality Brian Glenn had gotten married in Las Vegas. The pair had been dating for about 3 1/2 years.

“Last night, surrounded by our families, [Glenn] and I said ‘I do,’” Greene wrote on X, alongside a series of photos showing the couple exchanging vows at the Terrazza di Sogno, the Bellagio Resort’s outdoor wedding venue.

The Las Vegas Review-Journal reported that Greene and Glenn ― a former White House correspondent for Real America’s Voice ― had secured their marriage license in downtown Las Vegas last Friday.

The outlet also shared select details about the ceremony, noting that Greene walked down the aisle to Alex Warren’s “Ordinary.” Later, Ed Sheeran’s “Perfect” was played for family members and well-wishers, and Frank Sinatra’s rendition of “Fly Me To The Moon” capped off the nuptials.

According to People, Greene, 52, and Glenn, 56, met in 2022, and began dating about a year later, after they each filed for divorce from their spouses at the time. They publicly confirmed their engagement in December of last year.

Greene was previously married to Perry Greene for 27 years, with whom she shares three children. Glenn was formerly married to Kerry Michelle Glenn.

“People don’t see the side of Marjorie that I do,” Glenn told The Washington Post last year. “When you take her out of politics, she’s sweet. She’s sweet!”

Though the couple’s wedding has been widely characterized as an elopement, Glenn had dropped hints on social media in the days leading up to the ceremony.

“The clock is ticking,” he wrote on X alongside a photo of him and Greene sharing a kiss on the Las Vegas Strip.

For years, Greene was a staunch supporter of President Donald Trump and his Make America Great Again movement. She began to find herself frequently at-odds with Trump during his second term, starting with her push to release the files related to late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, who was friends with the president.

As her feud with Trump intensified, Greene resigned from Congress in January, calling the MAGA movement “a lie” and apologizing for her role in “toxic politics.” In June, she announced she was “done” with the GOP ― which she said Trump had turned into the “America Last party” ― altogether.

Glenn confirmed in May he was stepping away from Real America’s Voice. Unlike Greene, Glenn didn’t denounce Trump in his announcement, but nonetheless said he felt it was “time to leave the gloves in the ring and walk away.”
